strongest_angle: Examine the U.S. Army administrative investigation findings regarding the January 29, 2025 midair collision involving a UH-60L Black Hawk helicopter near Washington, D.C., which killed 67 people and revealed critical vulnerabilities across the International Civil Aviation Organization conflict management layers.

key_facts.fact: On January 29, 2025, a UH-60L Black Hawk helicopter with call sign PAT 25, assigned to the 12th Aviation Battalion, was involved in a midair collision near Washington, D.C., as detailed in the administrative investigation led by LTG Laura Potter.

The U.S. Army investigation into the midair collision near Washington, D.C., found that 67 people were killed following the convergence of multiple systemic failures between a Black Hawk helicopter and a civilian airliner.

The International Civil Aviation Organization leverages three layers of conflict management—Airspace Structure, Air Traffic Control Separation, and Collision Avoidance Technology—which all exhibited critical vulnerabilities during the January 29, 2025 incident.

numbers.label: Total fatalities in the midair collision
